quote: Like, it it goes under 15%? I don't seem to understand what you mean by that.
stewart_read: Rep doesn't grasp the customer's question on first pass, requiring the customer to re-explain three more times across the call.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep could have been intentionally slowing down to get precise details before answering, rather than genuinely confused.
coaching_implication: Coach active listening on technical questions — paraphrase back the customer's concern once before asking for repeated clarification, to avoid the customer feeling unheard.

quote: Yeah. That's a great question. So like I said, a lot of it is because, you know, on those days when it is producing, a lot of that gets used up in real time.
stewart_read: Rep repeats the identical explanation given at 01:47 almost word for word instead of adjusting to the customer's follow-up detail about the trimmed tree and low draw appliances.
alternative_hypothesis: Repetition could be a deliberate simplification technique to reinforce the point for an older customer who may not have grasped it the first time.
coaching_implication: When a customer pushes back on an explanation with new specifics (tree trimmed, low draw appliances), the rep should address the new detail directly rather than replaying the same line — otherwise it reads as not listening.

quote: So, like I said, I honestly wouldn't know. I'm not really sure what's being used in the home other than what you told me or, like, the production on those days.
stewart_read: Rep transparently admits the limits of his knowledge rather than fabricating a technical answer — this is the correct move per schema's 'admit and recover with transparency' path.
coaching_implication: This is a positive example to reinforce: admitting a gap and redirecting (to the battery offer, then to the specialist) is better than guessing. Praise this instinct even though the original question was never closed out.

quote: Have you considered looking into a battery backup system to store energy yourself rather than relying on ComEd for that?
stewart_read: Rep successfully identifies the customer's frustration with production/banking as a battery-backup opportunity and introduces it cleanly — this is a cross-sell catch, not a miss, but it's worth flagging as the pivotal moment that rescued the call.
alternative_hypothesis: Could be read as the rep changing the subject to avoid admitting he doesn't fully know the technical answer, rather than a deliberate value-add pivot.
coaching_implication: This pivot is the reason the call ends productively. Manager should note this as a repeatable move: when a technical question stalls, pivot to a relevant paid offering rather than continuing to loop on an unanswerable point.

quote: Kate is the one that originally helped you out get the solar system. He could actually give you a callback as early as Tuesday and actually discuss with you what a battery would look like
stewart_read: Rep routes the battery consultation to the original specialist rather than trying to close pricing/benefits himself, holding appropriate scope for a topic he's already shown gaps in.
coaching_implication: Reinforce this as correct scope discipline — the rep recognized he couldn't fully answer 'is it worth it' and routed to the person equipped to close it, rather than attempting to sell the battery on the spot.

quote: What is going to the electric company?
stewart_read: This is the customer's clearest, most concrete question of the call — asking directly about net metering/banking — and it's an opening to build curiosity about the battery's exact value. The rep answers factually (excess goes to grid) but doesn't connect it back to a concrete reason to act until two minutes later.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may have been holding the battery pitch deliberately until he had established the full context (ComEd's buyback rate) rather than rushing it, which is what he does at 06:06 — a strategic sequencing rather than a miss.
coaching_implication: Note as ambiguous: the delay between the customer's banking question and the battery pivot is short (under 2 minutes) and the rep does connect them via the buyback-rate framing, so this is a minor timing note rather than a hard miss.
